title: 15 convicted over Easter attacks get sentences ranging from 200 to 260 years
byline: The High Court Trial-at-Bar today sentenced 15 accused convicted over the 2019 Easter Sunday terror attacks to prison terms ranging from 200 to 260 years.

title: Govt. gazettes ‘Protection of the State from Terrorism’ Bill to replace PTA
byline: The Government has gazetted the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, which is intended to repeal and replace Sri Lanka’s long-standing Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act, No. 48 of 1979.

title: Dickwella returns to T20I Squad after five years
byline: Niroshan Dickwella earned a call-up to Sri Lanka’s T20I squad for the first time in half a decade as the country’s cricket board announced the squad for the Asian Games men’s cricket competition on Tuesday.

title: Suspect arrested over Rs. 24.85 Billion foreign currency transfer
byline: A 35-year-old man has been arrested in Wellampitiya in connection with an investigation into the alleged illegal transfer of foreign currency reserves worth Rs. 24.85 billion out of Sri Lanka, police said.

title: Catholic Church  expects satisfactory judgements on other cases pertaining to Easter Sunday attacks
byline: The Catholic Church  expects satisfactory judgements on other cases pertaining to the Easter Sunday bomb attacks, National Mass Communications Director Fr. Jude Krishantha said.

title: Trump threatens to annihilate Iran as diplomats push for deal at UN
byline: US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement ​could come soon amid a diplomatic push at the United Nations.

title: CBSL orders asset freeze on six companies
byline: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has imposed freezing orders on six companies and their directors, restricting them from transferring, disposing of or otherwise dealing with their properties and assets.

title: Fitch upgrade lifts CSE as ASPI rebounds above 21,000
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange rebounded on 22 September 2026, with both benchmark indices closing higher after sentiment improved sharply during the afternoon following Fitch’s upgrade of Sri Lanka’s sovereign rating from CCC+ to B- with a Stable Outlook.

title: US and Iran hold first talks since June after Trump’s ’annihilation’ threat
byline: Top Iranian and US officials have held talks at the UN in New York on a day when the US leader said he could ’’annihilate’’ the Islamic Republic if the conflict went unresolved.

title: Inquiry launched into clash between Harak Kata and Kehelbaddara Padme
byline: The Department of Prisons has launched a special investigation into a clash between two inmates identified as alleged organised crime figures, Nadun Chinthaka Wickremeratne, alias “Harak Kata”, and Mandinu Padmasiri, alias “Kehelbaddara Padme”, at the Welisara Prison.

title: Speaker endorses Bill to repeal  post of Chief of Defence Staff
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today announced that he has endorsed the Bill to repeal the post of Chief of Defence Staff.

title: Three new High Court Judges appointed
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake today appointed three new High Court Judges, with their letters of appointment formally handed over at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: Inclement weather in central hills
byline: Heavy rain experienced in the central hills persisted yesterday causing fear of landslides and earth slips in several areas.

title: 22A to be approved by Parliament on Friday
byline: Following the Supreme Court’s determination that a referendum is not required for the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, Parliament is set to approve the Bill on Friday (25) with a two-thirds majority, following a two-day debate.

title: IMF urges Sri Lanka to stay the course on economic reforms
byline: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) staff team has concluded a visit to Sri Lanka, with discussions focusing on recent economic developments, progress under the IMF Extended Fund Facility (EFF) programme and policy recommendations under the 2026 Article IV Consultation.

title: Court reduces sentence of couple convicted of procuring Russian woman
byline: The Court of Appeal yesterday reduced the seven-year prison sentences imposed on a husband and wife convicted of trafficking and procuring a Russian national for prostitution in Sri Lanka to four years, taking into special consideration the circumstances of their children.

title: Couple arrested as assets worth Rs. 47.5 Mn frozen in money laundering probe
byline: A 47-year-old man and his 45-year-old wife have been arrested in Padavi Parakramapura in connection with a money laundering investigation, while assets worth more than Rs. 47.5 million have been placed under a 14-day freezing order.

title: Driving licence medicals go digital from tomorrow
byline: A new digital system for issuing medical certificates required to obtain driving licences will be introduced from tomorrow (24), National Institute of Transport Medicine Chairman Prof. Clifford Perera said.

title: 5,741-km elephant fence gets major resource boost
byline: The Government has launched a major programme to strengthen the resources available to wildlife officials responsible for maintaining Sri Lanka’s 5,741-kilometre electric fence network, as part of a long-term strategy to address the country’s human-elephant conflict.

title: Oil holds near two-week lows while diesel cracks hit record peak
byline: Oil prices held near their lowest in more than two weeks ​on Wednesday as improving Gulf crude supplies weighed on the market, though diesel refining margins hit a ‌record high on potential restrictions to US diesel exports.

title: Sri Lanka Customs to enter paperless era from October 1
byline: Sri Lanka Customs is set to officially launch its first paperless customs declaration system on October 1, marking a major step towards the digital transformation of customs procedures and services to the trading community.

title: Ex-Maldives President Nasheed offers help in Sivarasa Anojan case
byline: Former Maldivian President Mohamed Nasheed has offered assistance in the case of Sri Lankan national Sivarasa Anojan, who faces a death sentence in Saudi Arabia.

title: More than 170,000 respiratory cases recorded in haze-choked Indonesia
byline: Some 175,000 people in Indonesia have suffered from respiratory illness since August, its health ministry said, as it continues to battle wildfires that have raged for weeks.

title: Namal Rajapaksa further remanded
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa was further remanded until September 30 by the Fort Magistrate’s Court today over allegations of money laundering in connection with the Airbus deal.

title: CAA cracks down on baby diaper imports without importer details
byline: Two businesses have been fined after being found distributing imported baby diapers without mandatory information identifying the registered importer.

title: Sri Lanka lost 10,000 foreign jobs due to corruption, poor handling: SLBFE Chairman
byline: Sri Lanka lost a significant number of foreign employment opportunities due to corrupt practices and poor handling of overseas job opportunities during the previous government, Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) Chairman Kosala Wickramasinghe said.

title: Route permits of buses found running on kerosene to be suspended
byline: The route permits of buses found to be operating on kerosene instead of diesel will be temporarily suspended, authorities said.

title: UK digital expertise and Sri Lankan business leaders unite to explore growth through technology
byline: Against the backdrop of mobile data usage increasing to 1.03 terabytes during the second quarter of this year, the British High Commission has facilitated a forum between UK digital product consultancy Apadmi and Sri Lankan business leaders to explore how such digital engagement could be converted to productive economic activities, according to a statement from the High Commission.

title: CSE extends rebound as ASPI holds above 21,000
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its recovery on 23 September 2026, with both benchmark indices closing higher for a second consecutive session despite some late profit-taking.

title: Deep depression to cross coastal areas of India tonight: Met. Department
byline: The Meteorology Department said the Deep Depression over the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal is likely to move west-northwestwards and cross the coastal areas of northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, India, during tonight.

title: Sectoral Oversight Committee approves 22A, Judicature Amendment Bills
byline: The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection has approved the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution and the Judicature (Amendment) Bills, which are scheduled for debate in Parliament on September 24 and 25.

title: Parliament approves Rs. 17.2 bn supplementary estimate for electricity relief
byline: Parliament today approved Supplementary Estimate No. 05 of 2026, under the Ministry of Energy, providing Rs. 17,213 million in financial assistance to offer relief to the public on electricity bills.

title: Public assistance sought to trace suspect wanted for child abuse
byline: Police have sought public assistance to identify and apprehend a suspect wanted in connection with the abduction and sexual abuse of a 13-year-old girl at Galle Face Green within the Fort Police Division on January 23, 2026.

title: BASL calls for conscience vote by MPs on 22A
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has called upon all the political parties in Parliament to allow the Members of Parliament to speak and vote on the 22nd amendment according to their conscience.

title: MP urges action over schoolchildren’s participation in LTTE cadre commemoration
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Chanaka Madugoda today urged the Government to take action against those responsible for involving schoolchildren in a commemoration event for former LTTE cadre Thileepan in the North.
